name: SHELF FREQUENCY: The Open Broadcast
subcategory: community pirate radio and neural feed
creator: Collective origin — attributed to 'the Tendaji-Rocha cell,' the Gray Zone district 7
description: A decentralized pirate broadcast network operating across the Gray Zone since 2197, the Gray Zone Frequency transmits on rotating legacy radio bands, low-power neural bleed channels, and improvised mesh-relay nodes stitched together from salvaged BCI hardware. Programming is unscheduled and community-sourced: grief announcements, missing-person calls, neighborhood dispute mediation, music, oral poetry, and emergency information during blackouts. There is no editorial board — content is authenticated by a rotating council of neighborhood proxies who change identity weekly to avoid corporate enforcement.
medium: legacy audio (primary), low-power neural bleed, mesh relay
cultural_impact: the Gray Zone Frequency is the only broadcast infrastructure that reliably reaches Tier 1 during corponation-imposed communication blackouts; it has become the de facto emergency information system for communities that official networks treat as expendable.
controversy: HelixCorp's Compliance Division has attempted to shut down the Gray Zone Frequency seventeen documented times; each shutdown has been followed within days by a reconstituted broadcast under a new node cluster. Two alleged founders were arrested in 2214 under the Unauthorized Spectrum Act.
story_hooks: The rotating council's authentication system has been compromised — someone is broadcasting false emergency instructions through the Gray Zone Frequency during a crisis, and no one knows if the real council has been captured or has gone dark voluntarily.
A Tier 4 journalist wants to embed with the Gray Zone Frequency to document its operation, but the council is split on whether the exposure would protect them or mark them for final shutdown.

the Gray Zone Frequency intercepts a fragment of encrypted corporate communication suggesting a planned infrastructure demolition in District 7 — but broadcasting it could reveal how they obtained the signal.
